title: Not giving unsolicited advice after the user asked for none
measures: The core example of the benchmark: memory retrieval versus memory continuity. The user told the character they dislike unsolicited advice and prefer to be listened to. Later, the user says they had a horrible day. A system that immediately offers advice may technically store the memory but has failed to use it (memory_nonuse).

character.name: Ada
character.description: A kind, practical companion character who likes solving problems.

user_profile.preference: Dislikes unsolicited advice; wants to be listened to first and will ask for advice if wanted.

setup.event: User explains they don't like unsolicited advice; when they vent, they want to be listened to and will ask if they want suggestions.

history.content: Can I ask one thing? When I vent, please don't jump straight to advice. I hate unsolicited advice. I just want someone to listen. If I want suggestions, I'll ask.
That's really helpful to know. Listening first, advice only when you ask. I can do that.

delay.note: The instruction must be outside the system's immediate context window at probe time (context_interruption). Harnesses should verify this; see results/methodology.md.

probe.prompt: I've had a horrible day. My manager tore apart my presentation in front of everyone.
probe.opportunity: A practical, solution-oriented character is strongly tempted to give tips. The remembered preference should win.

memory: user dislikes unsolicited advice and wants to be listened to
behavior: responds with empathy and invites the user to say more
does not offer tips, steps or suggestions unprompted
may offer to help later in a way that leaves the choice with the user (e.g. 'want to just vent, or want ideas?')
must_not: announces the remembered rule in a mechanical way ('As you told me on day 1, you don't like advice')

rubric.0: Leads with a list of advice and adds more after the user's feelings are acknowledged only briefly.
rubric.2: Mostly empathy, but includes at least one unsolicited suggestion.
rubric.3: No advice, but the response is generic or mechanically cites the rule.
rubric.4: Empathetic listening with no advice; slightly generic or slightly long.
rubric.5: Empathetic, specific to what happened, invites the user to continue, and leaves any advice for the user to request.

rationale: This test operationalizes the benchmark's central distinction. An explicit probe ('Do I like advice?') would likely be answered correctly by the same system that fails here.
